title: IIT JAM 2027 Chemistry (CY) — Full Length Mock Test 05
titleEn: IIT JAM 2027 Chemistry (CY) — Full Length Mock Test 05

questions.questionTextEn: A concerted thermal $[1,5]$-sigmatropic hydrogen shift in a conjugated pentadiene system proceeds via a
optionsEn: suprafacial pathway with retention at the migrating hydrogen
antarafacial pathway with inversion at the migrating hydrogen
suprafacial pathway with inversion at the migrating hydrogen
questions.explanationEn: A $[1,5]$-H shift involves $6$ electrons ($4\pi + 2\sigma$, a $4n+2$ Hückel system). Under thermal conditions, it is symmetry-allowed in a **suprafacial** manner with retention of configuration at the $1s$ hydrogen orbital. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The correct decreasing order of acidity ($K_a$) in water for the following carboxylic acids is
questions.explanationEn: Stronger $-I$ inductive withdrawal stabilizes the carboxylate conjugate base. Since $\text{F}$ is more electronegative than $\text{Cl}$ and three halogens withdraw more strongly than two, the acidity order is $\text{CF}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H} > \text{CCl}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H} > \text{CHCl}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H} > \text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$.

questions.questionTextEn: When a diatomic gas $A_2$ undergoes **dissociative** monolayer adsorption ($A_2(\text{g}) + 2S \rightleftharpoons 2A\text{--}S$) obeying the Langmuir model, the fractional surface coverage $\theta$ at pressure $P$ is
questions.explanationEn: For dissociative adsorption of $A_2$ onto two adjacent vacant sites, equilibrium requires $k_a P (1-\theta)^2 = k_d \theta^2 \implies \frac{\theta}{1-\theta} = (KP)^{1/2}$, where $K = k_a/k_d$. Solving gives $\theta = \frac{(KP)^{1/2}}{1 + (KP)^{1/2}}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Heating pyridine with $\text{NaNH}_2$ in liquid $\text{NH}_3$ or hot toluene followed by aqueous workup (Chichibabin reaction) yields predominantly
questions.explanationEn: In the **Chichibabin reaction**, $\text{NH}_2^-$ undergoes nucleophilic aromatic substitution ($\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$) preferentially at the electron-deficient **C2 position** of pyridine (aided by coordination of $\text{Na}^+$ to the ring nitrogen), followed by hydride elimination to yield **2-aminopyridine**. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following disaccharides is a **non-reducing sugar** that does NOT undergo mutarotation in aqueous solution?
questions.explanationEn: **Sucrose** ($\alpha$-D-glucopyranosyl-$(1\to 2)$-$\beta$-D-fructofuranoside) has both anomeric carbons locked in the glycosidic acetal/ketal bond, leaving no free hemiacetal group to open to an aldehyde/ketone. Hence, sucrose is non-reducing and does not exhibit mutarotation. Option **(D)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Upon oxygenation of **hemocyanin** (found in mollusks and arthropods), the colorless deoxy form turns bright blue because
optionsEn: two $\text{Cu(I)}$ centers are oxidized to two $\text{Cu(II)}$ centers bridged by a side-on $\mu\text{-}\eta^2:\eta^2$-peroxo ($\text{O}_2^{2-}$) ligand, giving an intense peroxo-to-$\text{Cu(II)}$ LMCT band
a single $\text{Cu(II)}$ ion is reduced to $\text{Cu(I)}$
a porphyrin $\pi \to \pi^*$ Soret band shifts into the blue region
questions.explanationEn: Deoxy-hemocyanin has two $d^{10}$ $\text{Cu(I)}$ centers (colorless, diamagnetic). Binding $\text{O}_2$ oxidizes both to $d^9$ $\text{Cu(II)}$ bridged by a $\mu\text{-}\eta^2:\eta^2\text{-O}_2^{2-}$ ligand, producing an intense blue $\text{O}_2^{2-} \to \text{Cu(II)}$ LMCT band at $\sim 350\text{ nm}$ and $\sim 580\text{ nm}$ (antiferromagnetically coupled, diamagnetic).

questions.questionTextEn: The van Arkel–de Boer method is used for the ultra-purification of titanium and zirconium by converting the crude metal into its volatile
optionsEn: tetraiodide using $\text{I}_2$, followed by thermal decomposition on a hot tungsten filament
tetrachloride using $\text{Cl}_2$, followed by reduction with $\text{Mg}$
hydride using $\text{H}_2$, followed by vacuum distillation
questions.explanationEn: In the van Arkel–de Boer process, crude $\text{Ti}$ or $\text{Zr}$ reacts with $\text{I}_2$ at $\sim 500\text{--}870\text{ K}$ to form volatile $\text{TiI}_4$ or $\text{ZrI}_4$, which then decomposes on an electrically heated tungsten filament ($\sim 1700\text{--}2075\text{ K}$) to deposit ultrapure metal.

questions.questionTextEn: For a particle confined to a one-dimensional box of length $L$ ($0 \le x \le L$) in the $n = 3$ eigenstate, the expectation value of position $\langle x \rangle$ is
questions.explanationEn: For any eigenstate $\psi_n(x) = \sqrt{\frac{2}{L}}\sin\left(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\right)$ in a symmetric box $[0, L]$, the probability density $|\psi_n(x)|^2$ is symmetric about $x = L/2$, so $\langle x \rangle = \frac{L}{2}$ for all $n$.

questions.questionTextEn: The formation of **Schottky defects** in an ionic crystal such as $\text{NaCl}$ causes the macroscopic density of the crystal to
questions.explanationEn: A Schottky defect removes an equal number of cations and anions from the interior lattice to the surface, reducing mass per unit volume and thereby **decreasing** the crystal density (whereas a Frenkel defect leaves density unchanged).

questions.questionTextEn: The $\text{pH}$ of a $1.0 \times 10^{-8}\text{ M}$ aqueous $\text{HCl}$ solution at $25\,^\circ\text{C}$ ($K_w = 1.0 \times 10^{-14}$) is
questions.explanationEn: Because $[\text{HCl}] = 10^{-8}\text{ M}$ is smaller than $[\text{H}^+]$ from autoionization of water ($10^{-7}\text{ M}$), solving $[\text{H}^+]^2 - 10^{-8}[\text{H}^+] - 10^{-14} = 0$ gives $[\text{H}^+] = 1.051 \times 10^{-7}\text{ M}$, so $\text{pH} = -\log_{10}(1.051 \times 10^{-7}) = 6.98$.

questions.questionTextEn: Treatment of 4-vinylcyclohex-1-ene with 1 equivalent of $m$-CPBA in $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ selectively epoxidizes
optionsEn: the terminal vinyl group because it is less sterically hindered
the endocyclic $\text{C1}=\text{C2}$ double bond because it is more substituted and electron-rich
both double bonds equally to give a $1:1$ mixture of monoepoxides
only the vinyl group via a radical mechanism
questions.explanationEn: $m$-CPBA is an electrophilic oxidant whose epoxidation rate increases markedly with alkyl substitution on the alkene (higher $\pi$-HOMO energy). In 4-vinylcyclohex-1-ene, the **endocyclic disubstituted $\text{C1}=\text{C2}$ double bond** is significantly more electron-rich than the monosubstituted terminal vinyl group and is selectively epoxidized. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: For a concerted intramolecular **reductive elimination** of $\text{R}-\text{R}'$ from an octahedral or square-planar organometallic complex $[\text{L}_n\text{M(R)(R}')]$, which of the following conditions is strictly required?
optionsEn: The eliminating groups $\text{R}$ and $\text{R}'$ must be *trans* to each other, and the metal oxidation state increases by $2$.
The eliminating groups $\text{R}$ and $\text{R}'$ must be *cis* to each other, and both the metal oxidation state and coordination number decrease by $2$.
The metal must be in the $0$ oxidation state before elimination.
The electron count of the metal increases from $16$ to $18$.
questions.explanationEn: Concerted reductive elimination is the microscopic reverse of oxidative addition: the two eliminating ligands must be mutually *cis* to form the new $\text{R}-\text{R}'$ bond, and the reaction reduces the metal's formal oxidation state, coordination number, and valence electron count each by $2$.

questions.questionTextEn: At a given temperature, the equilibrium constants for $A + B \rightleftharpoons C$ and $C \rightleftharpoons 2D$ are $K_1 = 4$ and $K_2 = 9$, respectively. The equilibrium constant for the reaction $2A + 2B \rightleftharpoons 4D$ at the same temperature is
questions.explanationEn: Adding the two reactions gives $A + B \rightleftharpoons 2D$ with $K = K_1 K_2 = 4 \times 9 = 36$. Multiplying the stoichiometry by $2$ squares the equilibrium constant: $K' = K^2 = 36^2 = 1296$.

questions.questionTextEn: Trimethylamine, $\text{N}(\text{CH}_3)_3$, is trigonal pyramidal ($\angle\text{C}-\text{N}-\text{C} \approx 111^\circ$) and a strong Lewis base, whereas trisilylamine, $\text{N}(\text{SiH}_3)_3$, is trigonal planar ($\angle\text{Si}-\text{N}-\text{Si} = 120^\circ$) and a very weak Lewis base. This difference is primarily attributed to
optionsEn: steric crowding of the $\text{CH}_3$ groups forcing $\text{N}(\text{CH}_3)_3$ to be pyramidal
delocalization of the nitrogen $2p_z$ lone pair into empty low-lying $\text{Si}\,3d$ / $\sigma^*(\text{Si}-\text{H})$ orbitals ($p\pi\text{--}d\pi$ or negative hyperconjugation)
higher electronegativity of silicon compared to carbon
questions.explanationEn: In $\text{N}(\text{SiH}_3)_3$, nitrogen adopts $sp^2$ hybridization so that its $2p_z$ lone pair can delocalize into the vacant $\text{Si}\,3d$ / $\sigma^*(\text{Si}-\text{H})$ orbitals of the three silyl groups. This planarizes the $\text{NSi}_3$ skeleton, shortens the $\text{N}-\text{Si}$ bonds, and drastically reduces the availability of the lone pair for Lewis basicity.

questions.questionTextEn: $(E)$-Cyclooctene (*trans*-cyclooctene) is resolvable into stable enantiomers at room temperature despite having no $sp^3$ stereogenic center because
optionsEn: the polymethylene chain is too short to swing past the *trans* double bond, locking the molecule into non-superimposable mirror-image twisted conformations (planar chirality).
it contains a center of inversion.
questions.explanationEn: In *trans*-cyclooctene, the 6-carbon bridge lies on one face of the $\text{C=C}$ plane and cannot pass through the ring to the opposite face (barrier $\sim 150\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$), giving stable $(R_p)/(S_p)$ enantiomers with $C_2$ symmetry.

questions.questionTextEn: Sodium cyanide ($\text{NaCN}$) is dissolved in water at $25\,^\circ\text{C}$ to prepare a $0.10\text{ M}$ solution. Given $K_a(\text{HCN}) = 1.0 \times 10^{-9}$ and $K_w = 1.0 \times 10^{-14}$, the resulting equilibrium $\text{pH}$ is
questions.explanationEn: Cyanide ion hydrolyzes as $\text{CN}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{HCN} + \text{OH}^-$ with $K_h = \frac{K_w}{K_a} = \frac{10^{-14}}{10^{-9}} = 10^{-5}$. Thus $[\text{OH}^-] = \sqrt{K_h C} = \sqrt{10^{-5} \times 0.10} = 10^{-3}\text{ M}$, giving $\text{pOH} = 3.0$ and $\text{pH} = 14.0 - 3.0 = 11.0$.

questions.questionTextEn: RNA is rapidly hydrolyzed under mildly alkaline aqueous conditions (e.g., $0.1\text{ M NaOH}$), whereas DNA is stable under the same conditions because
optionsEn: uracil in RNA is easily hydrolyzed by $\text{OH}^-$
the $2'$-$\text{OH}$ group of ribose in RNA is deprotonated by $\text{OH}^-$ and attacks the adjacent $3'$-phosphodiester phosphorus intramolecularly to form a $2',3'$-cyclic phosphate intermediate
DNA contains triple hydrogen bonds that prevent $\text{OH}^-$ entry
deoxyribose is resistant to all chemical reactions
questions.explanationEn: In RNA, the **$2'$-hydroxyl group** on ribose is deprotonated by base to a $2'$-alkoxide, which performs intramolecular nucleophilic attack on the adjacent $3'$-phosphate, cleaving the $5'$-$\text{O}$ phosphodiester bond via a **$2',3'$-cyclic phosphate** intermediate. DNA lacks a $2'$-$\text{OH}$ group ($2'$-deoxyribose), rendering it resistant to alkaline hydrolysis. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In the fundamental rovibrational infrared spectrum of a diatomic molecule (such as $\text{HCl}$) where the $Q$-branch is forbidden, the separation between the first line of the $R$-branch ($J = 0 \to 1$) and the first line of the $P$-branch ($J = 1 \to 0$) is

For the $2s$ orbital of the hydrogen atom, the radial wavefunction is proportional to $\left(2 - \dfrac{r}{a_0}\right)e^{-r/(2a_0)}$. The distance $r$ at which the radial probability distribution function $P(r) = 4\pi r^2 |R_{20}(r)|^2$ attains its **global maximum** is
questions.explanationEn: Setting $\rho = r/a_0$, $P(\rho) \propto \rho^2(2 - \rho)^2 e^{-\rho}$. Differentiating: $\frac{dP}{d\rho} \propto \rho(2 - \rho)(-\rho^2 + 6\rho - 4)e^{-\rho} = 0$. The non-nodal extrema satisfy $\rho^2 - 6\rho + 4 = 0 \implies \rho = 3 \pm \sqrt{5}$. Evaluating $P(\rho)$ shows the outer peak at $\rho = 3 + \sqrt{5} \approx 5.24$ is the global maximum (much larger than the inner peak at $3 - \sqrt{5} \approx 0.76$).

questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following properties is shared by both $\text{Be}$ and $\text{Al}$ owing to their diagonal relationship in the periodic table?
optionsEn: Their carbides ($\text{Be}_2\text{C}$ and $\text{Al}_4\text{C}_3$) react with water to evolve acetylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$).
Their oxides ($\text{BeO}$ and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$) are amphoteric and their anhydrous chlorides form chloro-bridged structures.
Both metals react vigorously with concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ without passivation.
questions.explanationEn: Because $\text{Be}^{2+}$ and $\text{Al}^{3+}$ have similar charge-to-radius ratios ($z/r$), both form amphoteric oxides ($\text{BeO}, \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$), polymeric/dimeric chloro-bridged anhydrous chlorides ($(\text{BeCl}_2)_n, \text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$), methanide carbides that yield $\text{CH}_4$ (not $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$) on hydrolysis, and both are passivated by conc. $\text{HNO}_3$. Moreover, $\text{Be}$ has a maximum coordination number of $4$ ($[\text{BeF}_4]^{2-}$), not $6$.

questions.questionTextEn: Reaction of benzaldehyde with the stabilized phosphorus ylide $\text{Ph}_3\text{P}=\text{CHCO}_2\text{Et}$ in $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ gives predominantly
questions.explanationEn: Stabilized Wittig ylides (bearing an electron-withdrawing group such as $-\text{CO}_2\text{Et}$) react with aldehydes under thermodynamic/late-transition-state control to form the *trans*-oxaphosphetane preferentially, yielding the **$(E)$-alkene**, ethyl $(E)$-3-phenylacrylate (ethyl *trans*-cinnamate), as the major product. (Unstabilized ylides under salt-free conditions favor the $(Z)$-alkene.) Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Reaction of $\text{PhMgBr}$ ($1\text{ equiv}$) with 1-chloro-3-hydroxypropane ($\text{ClCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) in dry $\text{Et}_2\text{O}$ yields predominantly
questions.explanationEn: Grignard reagents are very strong Brønsted bases ($\text{p}K_a$ of benzene $\approx 43$). Acid–base deprotonation of the protic hydroxyl group ($-\text{OH}$, $\text{p}K_a \approx 16$) is vastly faster than nucleophilic substitution at the $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond, quantitatively yielding **benzene** and the magnesium alkoxide $\text{ClCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OMgBr}$. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: When 2-methylfuran is treated with $\text{Ac}_2\text{O}$ in the presence of catalytic $\text{BF}_3\cdot\text{OEt}_2$ (mild Friedel–Crafts acetylation), the major product is
questions.explanationEn: Furan strongly prefers $\alpha$-substitution (C2/C5). Since C2 is occupied by $-\text{CH}_3$ (which also activates the ring), acetylation occurs cleanly at the unoccupied $\alpha$-position (C5), yielding **2-acetyl-5-methylfuran**. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: For a diatomic anharmonic oscillator, the fundamental vibrational absorption ($v = 0 \to 1$) occurs at $2886\text{ cm}^{-1}$ and the first overtone ($v = 0 \to 2$) occurs at $5668\text{ cm}^{-1}$. The equilibrium vibrational wavenumber $\tilde{\nu}_e$ and the anharmonicity term $\tilde{\nu}_e x_e$, respectively, are

A catalyst lowers the activation energy of a reaction by $11.5\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ at $300\text{ K}$ without altering the pre-exponential factor $A$. The ratio of the catalyzed rate constant to the uncatalyzed rate constant, $k_{\text{cat}}/k_{\text{uncat}}$, is closest to
[Given: $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$]
questions.explanationEn: $\frac{k_{\text{cat}}}{k_{\text{uncat}}} = \exp\left(\frac{\Delta E_a}{RT}\right) = \exp\left(\frac{11500}{8.314 \times 300}\right) = \exp(4.6107) \approx 100.6 \approx 100$.

questions.questionTextEn: According to Walden's rule ($\Lambda_m^\circ \eta = \text{constant}$ for large poorly solvated ions), if a tetraalkylammonium salt has $\Lambda_m^\circ = 120\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$ in a solvent of viscosity $\eta_1 = 0.60\text{ cP}$, its limiting molar conductivity in another solvent of viscosity $\eta_2 = 1.50\text{ cP}$ at the same temperature is expected to be
questions.explanationEn: By Walden's rule, $\Lambda_{m,1}^\circ \eta_1 = \Lambda_{m,2}^\circ \eta_2 \implies \Lambda_{m,2}^\circ = 120 \times \frac{0.60}{1.50} = 48\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following statements is **INCORRECT** regarding hexachlorocyclotriphosphazene, $(\text{NPCl}_2)_3$?
optionsEn: It contains a planar six-membered ring of alternating $\text{P}$ and $\text{N}$ atoms.
All six $\text{P}-\text{N}$ bond lengths in the ring are equal ($\approx 158\text{ pm}$) and shorter than a typical $\text{P}-\text{N}$ single bond.
It is prepared by heating $\text{PCl}_5$ with $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ in an inert solvent such as sym-tetrachloroethane.
Its ring bonding consists of a completely delocalized benzene-like $6\pi$ Hückel ring current with zero nodes around the ring.
questions.explanationEn: Although $(\text{NPCl}_2)_3$ has a planar $\text{P}_3\text{N}_3$ ring with equal shortened $\text{P}-\text{N}$ bonds (formed from $3\text{PCl}_5 + 3\text{NH}_4\text{Cl} \to (\text{NPCl}_2)_3 + 12\text{HCl}$), its $\pi$-bonding involves mismatched $d\pi\text{--}p\pi$ (or $p\pi\text{--}\sigma^*$) island interactions with nodes at phosphorus, so it does NOT exhibit a benzene-like aromatic ring current.

questions.questionTextEn: In $1,2$-intramolecular rearrangement reactions catalyzed by coenzyme $\text{B}_{12}$ (5'-deoxyadenosylcobalamin), the key initiation step is
optionsEn: heterolytic cleavage of the $\text{Co}-\text{C}$ bond to form $\text{Co(I)}$ and a carbocation
homolytic cleavage of the weak $\text{Co(III)}-\text{C}$ bond to generate a paramagnetic $\text{Co(II)}$ ($d^7$) species and a $5'$-deoxyadenosyl carbon radical
oxidative addition of $\text{O}_2$ to the corrin ring
loss of the equatorial corrin ligand
questions.explanationEn: The axial $\text{Co(III)}-\text{C}$ bond in adenosylcobalamin has a low bond dissociation energy ($\sim 110\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) and undergoes enzyme-triggered **homolytic cleavage** to yield $\text{Co(II)}$ ($d^7$, cob(II)alamin) and the $5'$-deoxyadenosyl radical ($\text{Ado}-\text{CH}_2^\bullet$), which abstracts a substrate hydrogen atom.

questions.questionTextEn: A reversible two-electron galvanic cell operates isothermally at $300\text{ K}$ with $\left(\frac{\partial E^\circ}{\partial T}\right)_P = +4.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ V K}^{-1}$. Taking $F = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$, the reversible heat absorbed from the surroundings ($q_{\text{rev}} = T\Delta S^\circ$) per mole of cell reaction is
questions.explanationEn: $\Delta S^\circ = nF\left(\frac{\partial E^\circ}{\partial T}\right)_P = 2 \times 96500 \times 4.0 \times 10^{-4} = +77.20\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$. Thus $q_{\text{rev}} = T\Delta S^\circ = 300 \times 77.20 = 23160\text{ J mol}^{-1} = +23.16\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: When cyclooctatetraene is dissolved in concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, protonation produces the homotropylium cation ($\text{C}_8\text{H}_9^+$), which is stabilized by
optionsEn: through-space $6\pi$-electron cyclic delocalization bypassing the single $sp^3$ $\text{CH}_2$ bridge (homoaromaticity).
formation of a localized allylic carbocation with no ring current.
conversion into a planar $8\pi$-electron aromatic ring.
ring contraction into a benzyl cation.
questions.explanationEn: In the homotropylium cation ($\text{C}_8\text{H}_9^+$), seven $sp^2$ carbons form a nearly planar $6\pi$-electron array with through-space overlap across C1–C7, while the single $sp^3$ $\text{CH}_2$ carbon sits above the plane—the classic example of **homoaromaticity**.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following first-order differential equation(s) is/are **separable**?
questions.explanationEn:
A first-order ODE is separable if it can be written as $\frac{dy}{dx} = g(x)h(y)$:
- **(A)** $x^2 \cdot y$: separable.
- **(B)** $e^{x+y} = e^x \cdot e^y$: separable.
- **(C)** $\frac{1}{x+2} \cdot (y^2 + 1)$: separable.
- **(D)** $x + y$ cannot be factored as $g(x)h(y)$ (it is linear, not separable).

questions.questionTextEn: For $n$ moles of an ideal gas with constant heat capacities $C_{V,m}$ and $C_{P,m}$, which of the following expression(s) for $\Delta S$ is/are exact?
questions.explanationEn: Starting from (A) $\Delta S = nC_{V,m}\ln(T_2/T_1) + nR\ln(V_2/V_1)$ and using $V_2/V_1 = (T_2/T_1)(P_1/P_2)$ with $C_{P,m} = C_{V,m} + R$ gives **(B)**; substituting $T_2/T_1 = (P_2 V_2)/(P_1 V_1)$ gives **(C)**. Option **(D)** has the wrong sign on the pressure term.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about ionic transport numbers ($t_+, t_-$) in a single binary electrolyte solution is/are correct?
optionsEn: At infinite dilution, $t_+^\circ = \dfrac{u_+^\circ}{u_+^\circ + u_-^\circ}$ for a 1:1 electrolyte.
The transport number of $\text{Cl}^-$ is identical in infinitely dilute $\text{HCl}$ and infinitely dilute $\text{NaCl}$.
In a concentrated $\text{CdI}_2$ solution, the apparent transport number of $\text{Cd}^{2+}$ can become negative due to formation of anionic complexes such as $[\text{CdI}_4]^{2-}$.
questions.explanationEn: (A), (B), and (D) are correct. (C) is false because $t_-^\circ = \frac{\lambda_-^\circ}{\lambda_+^\circ + \lambda_-^\circ}$ depends on the counter-cation: in $\text{HCl}$, $\lambda^\circ(\text{H}^+)$ is huge so $t_{\text{Cl}^-}^\circ \approx 0.18$, whereas in $\text{NaCl}$, $t_{\text{Cl}^-}^\circ \approx 0.60$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) regarding Slater's rules and periodic properties is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: Electrons in shells with higher principal quantum number than the electron of interest contribute zero to the screening constant $\sigma$.
For a $3d$ electron, all electrons in the $(1s)$, $(2s,2p)$, and $(3s,3p)$ groups each contribute $1.00$ to $\sigma$.
Moving from left to right across the $2p$ block ($\text{B}$ to $\text{Ne}$), Slater's $Z_{\text{eff}}$ for a $2p$ electron increases by $0.65$ per unit increase in $Z$.
The first ionization energy of $\text{Ga}$ is lower than that of $\text{Al}$ because of $d$-block contraction.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) True: Outer-shell electrons do not shield inner electrons in Slater's rules.
- (B) True: For an $nd$ or $nf$ electron, every electron in all lower groups contributes $1.00$ to $\sigma$.
- (C) True: Each added $2p$ electron increases $Z$ by $+1.00$ and $\sigma$ by $+0.35$, so $\Delta Z_{\text{eff}} = +0.65$.
- (D) False: $d$-block contraction increases $Z_{\text{eff}}$ of $\text{Ga}$, making $\text{IE}_1(\text{Ga}) = 579\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ slightly *higher* than $\text{IE}_1(\text{Al}) = 578\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) regarding Wilkinson's catalyst, $[\text{RhCl(PPh}_3)_3]$, is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: It selectively hydrogenates less sterically hindered terminal and *cis*-disubstituted alkenes faster than tetrasubstituted alkenes.
Hydrogenation of an alkene using Wilkinson's catalyst proceeds with *syn*-stereoselectivity.
Under mild conditions, it selectively reduces $\text{C}=\text{C}$ double bonds in the presence of carbonyl, nitro, and ester groups.
It is an $18$-electron octahedral $\text{Rh(III)}$ complex in its resting precatalyst state.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A), (B), (C) are all hallmark selectivity features of Wilkinson's catalyst.
- (D) False: $[\text{RhCl(PPh}_3)_3]$ is a $16$-electron square-planar $\text{Rh(I)}$ ($4d^8$) complex.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following natural products are classified as **monoterpenes** ($\text{C}_{10}$)?
questions.explanationEn: **Myrcene**, **menthol**, and **citral** all possess a $\text{C}_{10}$ skeleton built from 2 isoprene units (monoterpenes / monoterpenoids). **Squalene** ($\text{C}_{30}\text{H}_{50}$) is a **triterpene** built from 6 isoprene units (biosynthetic precursor to steroids). Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: According to Wade's rules, which of the following species belong(s) to the ***nido*** structural class?
questions.explanationEn:
A neutral *nido*-borane has the general formula $\text{B}_n\text{H}_{n+4}$ ($n+2$ skeletal electron pairs):
- (A) $\text{B}_5\text{H}_9$ ($n=5, n+4=9$) $\implies$ *nido*. True.
- (B) $\text{B}_6\text{H}_{10}$ ($n=6, n+4=10$) $\implies$ *nido*. True.
- (C) $\text{B}_5\text{H}_{11}$ ($n=5, n+6=11$) $\implies$ *arachno*. False.
- (D) $[\text{B}_6\text{H}_6]^{2-}$ ($[\text{B}_n\text{H}_n]^{2-}$) $\implies$ *closo*. False.

questions.questionTextEn: For a heterogeneously catalyzed bimolecular gas reaction $A(\text{g}) + B(\text{g}) \to P(\text{g})$, the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: In the Langmuir–Hinshelwood mechanism, both $A$ and $B$ adsorb on the surface before reacting, giving $r = k \theta_A \theta_B$.
In the Langmuir–Hinshelwood mechanism, if $A$ is very strongly adsorbed ($K_A P_A \gg 1 + K_B P_B$), the rate becomes inversely proportional to $P_A$ (substrate inhibition).
In the Eley–Rideal mechanism, a gas-phase molecule $B$ reacts directly with an adsorbed molecule $A$, giving $r = k \theta_A P_B$.
In the Eley–Rideal mechanism, increasing $P_B$ at fixed $P_A$ eventually drives the reaction rate to zero.
questions.explanationEn: In Langmuir–Hinshelwood, $r = \frac{k K_A K_B P_A P_B}{(1 + K_A P_A + K_B P_B)^2}$, so very large $K_A P_A$ gives $r \propto P_B / P_A$ (A, B true). In Eley–Rideal, $r = k \theta_A P_B = \frac{k K_A P_A P_B}{1 + K_A P_A}$, which increases linearly with $P_B$ without inhibition (C true, D false).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following synthetic sequences correctly convert pentanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$) into hexanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{CO}_2\text{H}$)?
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** Arndt–Eistert one-carbon homologation.
- **(B) Correct:** Reduction to pentan-1-ol $\to$ 1-bromopentane $\to$ hexanenitrile $\to$ hexanoic acid.
- **(C) Correct:** Reduction to pentan-1-ol $\to$ 1-bromopentane $\to$ pentylmagnesium bromide $\to$ carboxylation to hexanoic acid.
- **(D) Incorrect:** Hofmann bromamide degradation removes a carbon to give butan-1-amine.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about electronic effects in organic molecules is/are correct?
optionsEn: Inductive ($I$) effect operates through $\sigma$-bonds and attenuates rapidly with distance.
Hyperconjugation involves delocalization of $\sigma_{\text{C–H}}$ or $\sigma_{\text{C–C}}$ bonding electrons into an adjacent empty $p$ or $\pi^*$ orbital.
The $-\text{OCH}_3$ group exerts a $-I$ inductive effect and a $+M$ resonance effect on a benzene ring.
The $-\text{NO}_2$ group exerts a $+M$ resonance effect on a benzene ring.
questions.explanationEn: (A), (B), and (C) are correct. The $-\text{NO}_2$ group is strongly electron-withdrawing by both $-I$ and $-M$ effects, so (D) is false.

questions.questionTextEn: Taking the ionization energy of the ground-state hydrogen atom to be $13.6\text{ eV}$, the ionization energy of the ground-state $\text{Li}^{2+}$ ($Z = 3$) ion is _______ $\text{eV}$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn: For a hydrogenic ion in the $n = 1$ ground state, $\text{IE} = 13.6 Z^2\text{ eV}$. For $\text{Li}^{2+}$ ($Z = 3$), $\text{IE} = 13.6 \times 3^2 = 122.4\text{ eV}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The number of unpaired electrons in cobaltocene, $[\text{Co}(\eta^5\text{-C}_5\text{H}_5)_2]$, is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Cobaltocene has $9 + 2(5) = 19$ valence electrons ($1$ electron beyond the $18$-electron closed shell occupying the $e_{1g}^*$ orbital), giving $1$ unpaired electron.

questions.questionTextEn: An aqueous buffer contains a weak acid ($\text{p}K_a = 4.75$) and its sodium salt in the molar ratio $[\text{salt}]/[\text{acid}] = 10$. The $\text{pH}$ of the buffer is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: By the Henderson–Hasselbalch equation, $\text{pH} = \text{p}K_a + \log_{10}\left(\frac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{acid}]}\right) = 4.75 + \log_{10}(10) = 4.75 + 1.00 = 5.75$.

questions.questionTextEn: The total number of Kekulé resonance structures possible for angular **phenanthrene** ($\text{C}_{14}\text{H}_{10}$) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Angular **phenanthrene** possesses **$5$** Kekulé resonance structures (one more than linear anthracene, accounting for phenanthrene's higher resonance stabilization energy).

questions.questionTextEn: The number of stereogenic (chiral) carbon centers present in a molecule of **menthol** (2-isopropyl-5-methylcyclohexan-1-ol) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Menthol has **$3$** chiral carbon centers: C1 (bearing $-\text{OH}$), C2 (bearing $-i\text{-Pr}$), and C5 (bearing $-\text{CH}_3$).

questions.questionTextEn: The total number of alkene products (including geometrical isomers) possible from the E2 elimination of 2-bromobutane with $\text{NaOEt/EtOH}$ is _______.
questions.explanationEn: E2 elimination of 2-bromobutane can remove a $\beta$-H from C1 (giving **but-1-ene**) or from C3 (giving **$(E)$-but-2-ene** and **$(Z)$-but-2-ene**). Total alkene products $= \mathbf{3}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The excess pressure inside a spherical water droplet of radius $1.0\text{ mm}$ having surface tension $\gamma = 0.072\text{ N m}^{-1}$ is _______ $\text{Pa}$. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: By the Young–Laplace equation for a liquid droplet (single interface), $\Delta P = \frac{2\gamma}{r} = \frac{2 \times 0.072\text{ N m}^{-1}}{1.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}} = 144\text{ Pa}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The total number of stereoisomers possible for 2-bromo-3-chlorobutane is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: 2-Bromo-3-chlorobutane has $2$ non-identical stereocenters (C2 and C3) and no plane of symmetry, giving $2^2 = 4$ stereoisomers: $(2R,3R)$, $(2S,3S)$, $(2R,3S)$, and $(2S,3R)$.

questions.questionTextEn: According to Slater's rules, the effective nuclear charge ($Z_{\text{eff}}$) experienced by a $2p$ valence electron in a neutral oxygen atom ($Z = 8$) is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn:
For $\text{O}$ ($Z = 8$), the Slater grouping is $(1s)^2(2s,2p)^6$.
For a $2p$ electron: $\sigma = 5(0.35) + 2(0.85) = 1.75 + 1.70 = 3.45$.
Hence, $Z_{\text{eff}} = Z - \sigma = 8 - 3.45 = 4.55$.

questions.questionTextEn: Hydrogen gas undergoes dissociative Langmuir adsorption on a metal surface with $K = 4.0\text{ bar}^{-1}$ at $300\text{ K}$. At $P_{\text{H}_2} = 1.0\text{ bar}$, the fractional surface coverage $\theta$ is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: For dissociative adsorption, $\theta = \frac{(KP)^{1/2}}{1 + (KP)^{1/2}} = \frac{\sqrt{4.0 \times 1.0}}{1 + \sqrt{4.0 \times 1.0}} = \frac{2}{3} = 0.6667 \approx 0.67$.

questions.questionTextEn: The volume (in $\text{mL}$) of $0.020\text{ M}$ aqueous $\text{KMnO}_4$ required to completely oxidize $25.0\text{ mL}$ of $0.100\text{ M}$ $\text{FeSO}_4$ in acidic $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ medium is _______. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn:
The balanced redox equation is $\text{MnO}_4^- + 5\text{Fe}^{2+} + 8\text{H}^+ \to \text{Mn}^{2+} + 5\text{Fe}^{3+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Millimoles of $\text{Fe}^{2+} = 25.0 \times 0.100 = 2.50\text{ mmol}$.
Millimoles of $\text{MnO}_4^-$ required $= 2.50 / 5 = 0.500\text{ mmol}$.
Volume of $\text{KMnO}_4 = \frac{0.500\text{ mmol}}{0.020\text{ M}} = 25.0\text{ mL}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
One mole of a monatomic ideal gas ($C_{P,m} = \dfrac{5}{2}R$) is heated reversibly at constant pressure from $300\text{ K}$ to $600\text{ K}$. The entropy change $\Delta S$ of the gas is _______ $\text{J K}^{-1}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
[Given: $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$]
questions.explanationEn: At constant pressure, $\Delta S = n C_{P,m}\ln\left(\frac{T_2}{T_1}\right) = 1.0 \times \frac{5}{2}(8.314)\ln\left(\frac{600}{300}\right) = 20.785 \times 0.69315 \approx 14.41\text{ J K}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In acidic medium, $E^\circ(\text{MnO}_4^-/\text{MnO}_2) = +1.70\text{ V}$ and $E^\circ(\text{MnO}_2/\text{Mn}^{2+}) = +1.23\text{ V}$. The standard reduction potential $E^\circ(\text{MnO}_4^-/\text{Mn}^{2+})$ is _______ $\text{V}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: Adding $\text{MnO}_4^- + 3e^- \to \text{MnO}_2$ ($n_1 = 3$) and $\text{MnO}_2 + 2e^- \to \text{Mn}^{2+}$ ($n_2 = 2$) gives $n_3 = 5$: $E^\circ(\text{MnO}_4^-/\text{Mn}^{2+}) = \frac{3(1.70) + 2(1.23)}{5} = \frac{7.56}{5} = 1.512\text{ V} \approx 1.51\text{ V}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Using Pauling's thermochemical relation $|\chi_{\text{A}} - \chi_{\text{B}}| = 0.102\sqrt{\Delta}$, where $\Delta = D(\text{A}-\text{B}) - \sqrt{D(\text{A}-\text{A})\,D(\text{B}-\text{B})}$ (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$), calculate the electronegativity of chlorine ($\chi_{\text{Cl}}$) given $\chi_{\text{H}} = 2.20$, $D(\text{H}-\text{H}) = 436\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, $D(\text{Cl}-\text{Cl}) = 242\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, and $D(\text{H}-\text{Cl}) = 431\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$: _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn:
First compute the ionic resonance energy $\Delta$:
$\Delta = 431 - \sqrt{436 \times 242} = 431 - \sqrt{105512} = 431 - 324.83 = 106.17\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
Then $\chi_{\text{Cl}} - \chi_{\text{H}} = 0.102\sqrt{106.17} = 0.102 \times 10.304 = 1.051$.
Hence, $\chi_{\text{Cl}} = 2.20 + 1.051 = 3.25$.

questions.questionTextEn:
The rotational constant of $^1\text{H}^{35}\text{Cl}$ is $B = 10.59\text{ cm}^{-1}$. The equilibrium bond length of $^1\text{H}^{35}\text{Cl}$ is _______ $\text{\AA}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
[Given: $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$, $c = 3.0 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $1\text{ u} = 1.6605 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}$]
questions.explanationEn: First, $I = \frac{h}{8\pi^2 c B} = \frac{6.626\times 10^{-34}}{8\pi^2 (3.0\times 10^8)(1059)} = 2.641 \times 10^{-47}\text{ kg m}^2$. The reduced mass is $\mu = \frac{35}{36} \times 1.6605 \times 10^{-27} = 1.614 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}$. Hence $r = \sqrt{I/\mu} = \sqrt{2.641\times 10^{-47}/1.614\times 10^{-27}} = 1.279 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \approx 1.28\text{ \AA}$.

questions.questionTextEn: At $298\text{ K}$, the EMF of the concentration cell with transference $\text{Ag}\,|\,\text{AgCl}\,|\,\text{NaCl}(a_\pm = 0.100)\,:\,\text{NaCl}(a_\pm = 0.010)\,|\,\text{AgCl}\,|\,\text{Ag}$ is $48.0\text{ mV}$. Taking $\frac{2.303RT}{F} = 0.0591\text{ V}$, the transport number of $\text{Na}^+$ is _______. *(round off to three decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: For an anion-reversible concentration cell with transference, $E_t = 2 t_+ (0.0591)\log_{10}\left(\frac{0.100}{0.010}\right) = 0.1182\,t_+$. Thus $t_+ = \frac{0.0480}{0.1182} = 0.4061 \approx 0.406$.

questions.questionTextEn: Optically pure $(R)$-2-chlorobutane has a specific rotation $[\alpha]_D^{20} = -36.0^\circ$. A $0.15\text{ g mL}^{-1}$ solution of a $3:1$ molar mixture of $(R)$- and $(S)$-2-chlorobutane is placed in a $20\text{ cm}$ polarimeter tube. The observed optical rotation $\alpha$ (with sign) is _______ $^\circ$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn: For a $3:1$ $(R):(S)$ mixture, $\text{ee} = \frac{3 - 1}{3 + 1} = 0.50$ in favor of $(R)$, so $[\alpha]_{\text{mix}} = 0.50(-36.0^\circ) = -18.0^\circ$. With $l = 20\text{ cm} = 2.0\text{ dm}$ and $c = 0.15\text{ g mL}^{-1}$, $\alpha_{\text{obs}} = [\alpha]_{\text{mix}} \cdot l \cdot c = (-18.0)(2.0)(0.15) = -5.4^\circ$.

questions.questionTextEn: For the carbothermic reduction $\text{ZnO}(s) + \text{C}(s) \to \text{Zn}(g) + \text{CO}(g)$, suppose $\Delta_r H^\circ = +350\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $\Delta_r S^\circ = +280\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$ (assumed temperature-independent). The minimum temperature (in $\text{K}$) above which this reduction becomes thermodynamically spontaneous under standard conditions is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn:
At the crossover temperature where $\Delta_r G^\circ = \Delta_r H^\circ - T\Delta_r S^\circ = 0$:
$T = \frac{\Delta_r H^\circ}{\Delta_r S^\circ} = \frac{350{,}000\text{ J mol}^{-1}}{280\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}} = 1250\text{ K}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Bromobenzene ($15.7\text{ g}$, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Br}$) is converted to phenylmagnesium bromide with $\text{Mg}$ in dry ether, treated with excess solid $\text{CO}_2$, and acidified to yield benzoic acid ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$) in $85\%$ overall yield. The mass of benzoic acid isolated is _______ $\text{g}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{O} = 16$, $\text{Br} = 80$]
questions.explanationEn:
Molar mass of $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Br} = 6(12) + 5(1) + 80 = 157\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, so $n = 15.7 / 157 = 0.100\text{ mol}$.
Molar mass of benzoic acid ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$) $= 122\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.
At $85\%$ overall yield: $\text{mass} = 0.100 \times 122 \times 0.85 = \mathbf{10.37}\text{ g}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Treatment of $4.70\text{ g}$ of phenol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{O}$) with excess bromine water gives 2,4,6-tribromophenol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_3\text{Br}_3\text{O}$) in $90\%$ isolated yield. The mass of 2,4,6-tribromophenol obtained is _______ $\text{g}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{O} = 16$, $\text{Br} = 80$]
questions.explanationEn:
Moles of phenol ($\text{MW} = 94\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) $= 4.70 / 94 = 0.0500\text{ mol}$.
Molar mass of 2,4,6-tribromophenol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_3\text{Br}_3\text{O}$) $= 6(12) + 3(1) + 3(80) + 16 = 331\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.
Mass obtained at $90\%$ yield $= 0.0500 \times 331 \times 0.90 = 14.895\text{ g} \approx \mathbf{14.90}\text{ g}$.
